hop3_docs: Dispositive motion | In law, a dispositive motion is a motion seeking a trial court order entirely disposing of all or part of the claims in favor of the moving party without need for further trial court proceedings.  "To dispose" of a claim means to "decide" the claim in favor of one or another party.  As a lawsuit may comprise numerous claims made by and against numerous parties, not every dispositive motion seeks to dispose of the entire lawsuit.  In the U.S., the most common type of dispositive motions seeking to dispose of the entire lawsuit are those for summary judgment.  Many U.S. state jurisdictions also provide for a "partial summary judgment" or motion for "summary adjudication of issues" which only seeks to dispose of part of a lawsuit.  See, e.g., California Code of Civil Procedure section 437c(f)(1).
